title: How We Made TAKE 212 – Two Developers, Two AI Agents, and a Director Made of TVs
author: HiSebbo
selftext:
Hey everyone!

We took a short break from our main project and decided to try something completely different for the Epic AI MegaJam 2026.

Four days, two developers, two AI agents, and a lot of experimenting.

The result is **TAKE 212 – Director's Cut**, a surreal first-person parkour game with shifting realities, a strange world, and a director made of flying TVs.

**What came out of those four days:**

* \~40,000 lines of C++ across 64 files
* 91 automated tests
* 26 Python editor scripts
* 13 maps
* 92 director voice lines
* A trailer edited by AI

We used Unreal Engine 5.8, Claude Opus 5.5, Unreal MCP, Suno, and Qwen3-TTS.

What surprised us most wasn't really the speed. It was being able to try ideas we normally wouldn't even consider with such limited time.

The TV director is a good example. We were pretty skeptical about getting something like that working in four days, but decided to give it a shot anyway.

Not everything worked, of course. Animations, game feel, and getting things to actually look and play right still took plenty of work.

We also experimented with having AI edit our trailer without actually watching or hearing it, which was pretty interesting.

We wrote a full devlog about how we built everything, what worked, and what didn't. There's also a development trailer showing the process.

**Devlog + Trailer:**  
[https://reigen-games.itch.io/take-212/devlog/1779883/how-we-made-take-212-two-developers-two-ai-agents-and-a-director-made-of-tvs](https://reigen-games.itch.io/take-212/devlog/1779883/how-we-made-take-212-two-developers-two-ai-agents-and-a-director-made-of-tvs)

Would love to hear what you think, especially if you've been experimenting with AI agents in game development too!
